title: Human-facing plan
description: Data for template.html. Flat on purpose: top-level fields, one ordered list of blocks, one map of terms; no object sits deeper than a block. Text fields take three inline marks: **bold**, `code`, [[term]] or [[shown text|term]]. Plain fields (headings, names, labels, `when`, columns, steps) take no marks. No HTML anywhere; it is escaped. The main text assumes `reader`; what that reader may not know goes into `terms`.

lang.description: Language of the page's own labels: zh-CN for Chinese content, en for anything else. Write the content in the user's language.

title.description: What gets done, as a noun phrase.

kind.description: Document kind in the top bar, e.g. 开发方案, 活动方案, Launch plan. Defaults to 方案 / Plan.

project.description: Repo or product name in the top bar.

status.description: review while waiting for decisions; approved once the user confirms.

reader.description: Who the main text is written for. Default: smart, knows the domain, was not in this conversation, does not know the details. Infer it from the request; never ask.

summary.description: The conclusion in 1–3 sentences: what gets done, its scope, its cost. Not background.

decisions.description: What the reader has to decide. Omit when nothing is open. Each carries a recommendation; no reply means the recommendation is taken.

options.description: The first option is the recommendation. Each is "option | cost"; the cost is optional, e.g. "转为后台任务，完成后站内通知 | +1 天". Marks are allowed in the option text.

why.description: Why the recommendation, backed by a number or a fact. If this decision interacts with another, say how here.

blocks.description: The body, in reading order. An h2 starts a section: it sticks under the top bar while its section is on screen and becomes a contents entry; h3s become sub-entries. Consecutive option, row, step or flow blocks merge into one table, list or diagram.

terms.description: Term → explanation (1–3 plain sentences), shown as a side note beside the line that uses it. Mark the term's first use as [[term]], reading in this order: summary, then decisions (question, options, why), then blocks. Every key must be marked and every mark must have a key. Only explain what the reader may not know.

changelog.description: One line per revision, oldest first, e.g. "2026-10-10 初稿". The footer shows the last line.

plain.description: Plain text: no [[term]] marks; ** and ` show literally.

id.description: Stable anchor for links, e.g. "risks". Optional; "decide" is reserved.

list.description: Bullets, or numbered steps a user takes (ordered). For what is out of scope, one item per exclusion: "what: why not now".

table.description: A small table: sample data, a side-by-side comparison of two things, a mapping. Numeric columns right-align on their own. With `file`, it is drawn as a preview of that file.

rows.description: One string per row, cells separated by " | "; write a literal pipe as \|. Same number of cells as columns. Cells take marks.

file.description: File name, when the table shows the contents of a file.

fileTag.description: Short note on the file's header, e.g. 用 Excel 打开.

option.description: One row of an options-considered table: which way to do it. Consecutive option blocks form one table; exactly one is chosen. For comparing two things that are not alternatives (two vendors' behaviour), use a table.

reason.description: Chosen: the scope it covers. Rejected: the deal-breaker, in one line.

row.description: A label + text pair, for risks, costs, constraints. Consecutive rows form one list.

step.description: One step of the rollout plan. Consecutive steps form one list. For steps a user takes in the product, use an ordered list.

when.description: e.g. 第 1 天, 第 1–2 天, Week 2.

done.description: How anyone can tell the step is finished. The page adds the "done when" label.

flow.description: One path through states or stages, drawn as chips joined by arrows. Consecutive flows stack into one diagram, one path each; branch by writing another flow.

label.description: What the path belongs to, e.g. 批次 / Batch. Optional.

note.description: When this path happens, in one line.

check.description: A self-check right after the passage it tests; the answer stays hidden until clicked. Aim at the likeliest misreading, not at recall. At most 4 per document, often fewer. If the answer needs a long explanation, fix the passage instead.

answer.description: The correct answer in one sentence; shown in bold.

detail.description: Why the intuitive answer is wrong, in at most two sentences.

callout.description: At most one per section. warn: something to watch or that can bite at rollout. info: a cross-reference or roll-up, e.g. how each decision moves the estimate.

code.description: Literal code, a command, or a payload. Not for diagrams; use flow.
